subject_entity.title_display: De Dominica Oratione (On the Lord's Prayer)
subject_entity.notes: Cyprian's treatise on the Lord's Prayer c. 252; systematic exposition of each petition; emphasizes unity, the Eucharist as daily bread, forgiveness, and the communal nature of Christian prayer; heavily influenced by Tertullian's De Oratione but adds distinctly ecclesiological and eucharistic dimensions.

object_entity.notes: Bishop of Carthage c. 248–258; major Latin theologian of ecclesiology and sacramental theology; converted c. 246; deeply influenced by Tertullian; key figure in the Novatian controversy (supported Cornelius against Novatian); martyred under Valerian.

evidence.notes: Cyprian is the author of De Dominica Oratione.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Before all things, the Teacher of peace and Master of unity would not have prayer to be made singly and individually, as if a person prays only for himself alone. We do not say 'My Father who art in heaven' nor 'Give me this day my daily bread.' Our prayer is public and common; and when we pray, we pray not for one, but for the whole people, because we the whole people are one.
passage.notes: Communal nature of Christian prayer; 'Our Father' reflects ecclesial unity
